items.rule_line: Reviewing prior estimate outcomes informs the risk assessment about the estimation process and management bias.

why.A: Estimates involve uncertainty, so precise correctness is not the standard.
why.B: Prior accuracy does not remove the need to obtain evidence about current-year estimates.
why.C: Correct. Reviewing prior outcomes informs the auditor about estimation processes and possible bias and supports the risk assessment for current estimates.
why.D: The review is not a basis for restating prior periods; differences between estimates and outcomes are not necessarily errors.

guide.ask: Is the review of prior estimate outcomes meant to prove they were exact?
guide.reveal: No, differences are normal.

guide.ask: What is its purpose?
guide.reveal: To inform the auditor about the estimation process and possible bias for the current risk assessment.

items.group_name: Specific areas of engagement risk
items.blueprint: AUD.II.G Specific areas of engagement risk [II.G.3]
items.topic: Related party transactions and significant risk
items.task: Assess related parties as an area of engagement risk.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: The auditor of Stonebridge Farms, a nonissuer, learns that the company sold land outside its normal course of business to an entity owned by the CEO's brother at a price above the appraised value. How should the auditor assess this transaction?
options: As a significant risk, because it is a significant unusual transaction with a related party
As a risk relating only to disclosure, with no risk to the measurement of the transaction
As a significant risk only if the amount exceeds materiality for the financial statements as a whole
As a routine transaction, because the stated price is supported by a third-party appraisal
items.rule_line: Significant unusual related party transactions are significant risks.

why.A: Correct. Related party transactions that are also significant unusual transactions give rise to significant risks.
why.B: Related party transactions may be misstated in measurement, classification and disclosure.
why.C: Treatment as a significant risk does not depend on exceeding overall materiality.
why.D: A sale outside the normal course to a related party at an unexplained premium is not routine; the price supports no conclusion about business purpose.

guide.ask: What two features does the land sale have?
guide.reveal: It is outside the normal course of business and with a related party.

guide.ask: How does the auditor classify a transaction with both features?
guide.reveal: As a significant risk.

items.group_name: Specific areas of engagement risk
items.blueprint: AUD.II.G Specific areas of engagement risk [II.G.3]
items.topic: Records that indicate undisclosed related parties
items.task: Assess related parties as an area of engagement risk.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: During the audit of Greenfield Packaging, a nonissuer, the auditor remains alert for undisclosed related party relationships. Which records must the auditor specifically inspect for such indications?
options: Management's list of related parties, which is sufficient without inspecting any other records
The fixed asset register and depreciation schedules
The entity's federal tax returns for the last three years
Bank and legal confirmations, and minutes of shareholder and governance meetings
items.rule_line: Inspect bank and legal confirmations and governance minutes for undisclosed related party information.

why.A: The auditor cannot rely only on management's list; the required inspection exists because management may not have disclosed everything.
why.B: The fixed asset register is not one of the records specified for this purpose.
why.C: Tax returns are not among the records the standard specifies for this inspection.
why.D: Correct. The auditor inspects bank and legal confirmations and minutes of shareholder and governance meetings for undisclosed related parties.

guide.ask: Is management's list enough to identify related parties?
guide.reveal: No, the auditor inspects other records.

guide.ask: Which records must be inspected?
guide.reveal: Bank and legal confirmations, and minutes of shareholder and governance meetings.

items.group_name: Specific areas of engagement risk
items.blueprint: AUD.II.G Specific areas of engagement risk [II.G.4]
items.topic: Internal control over federal programs in a single audit
items.task: Understand requirements for single audits in accordance with the Uniform Guidance.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: In a single audit of Riverton County, the auditor obtains an understanding of internal control over federal programs. Which requirement applies to the auditor's testing of internal control over compliance for major programs?
options: Test internal control only if the auditor decides to reduce the extent of substantive compliance testing for those programs
Plan and perform control testing to support a low assessed control risk, unless controls are likely ineffective
Obtain an understanding of internal control, but testing is optional for all major programs
Test internal control only for the major programs with the largest expenditures
items.rule_line: In a single audit, plan and perform control testing over major programs to support low control risk, unless controls are likely ineffective.

why.A: Testing is required in a single audit whether or not the auditor plans to reduce compliance testing.
why.B: Correct. The auditor plans and performs testing of internal control over compliance to support a low assessed control risk, unless controls are likely ineffective.
why.C: Testing is required, not optional, except where controls are likely ineffective, in which case a deficiency is reported.
why.D: The requirement applies to compliance requirements of each major program, not only the largest.

guide.ask: What is the goal of testing internal control over compliance for major programs?
guide.reveal: Supporting a low assessed control risk.

guide.ask: When is testing not performed?
guide.reveal: Only when controls are likely ineffective.

items.group_name: Specific areas of engagement risk
items.blueprint: AUD.II.G Specific areas of engagement risk [II.G.4]
items.topic: Type A program threshold
items.task: Determine major programs under the Uniform Guidance.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: Waverly School District expended $40,000,000 in total federal awards during its fiscal year. In determining major programs for the single audit, the auditor identifies Type A programs. Federal programs whose expenditures exceed what amount are Type A?
items.rule_line: Type A threshold: $1 million up to $34 million of awards; 3% from $34 million to $100 million; then flat or lower percentages.

why.A: This applies 0.3% instead of 3% of total awards expended.
why.B: $1,000,000 is the Type A threshold for total awards of $34 million or less.
why.C: Correct. For total awards over $34 million up to $100 million, the Type A threshold is 3% of total awards expended: 3% x $40,000,000 = $1,200,000.
why.D: $3,000,000 is the flat threshold for total awards over $100 million up to $1 billion.

steps: $40,000,000 is over $34 million and up to $100 million

verify.note: 2 CFR 200.518(b)(1) eCFR 표 확인: 연방자금 $34M 초과~$100M 이하는 총액×0.03 = $1,200,000. 정답 C 유효.

guide.ask: Which total-awards band contains $40,000,000?
guide.reveal: Over $34 million up to $100 million.

guide.ask: What is the Type A threshold in that band?

items.group_name: Specific areas of engagement risk
items.blueprint: AUD.II.G Specific areas of engagement risk [II.G.4]
items.topic: Percentage of coverage for major programs
items.task: Determine major programs under the Uniform Guidance.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: In a single audit of Kestrel Public Health, the auditor identifies the Type A programs that are not low-risk and the high-risk Type B programs. Together they represent 27% of total federal awards expended. Kestrel does not qualify as a low-risk auditee. What must the auditor do?
options: Nothing more, because 20% coverage is enough once the required programs are audited
Audit additional programs so that the major programs cover at least 50% of total federal awards expended
Audit additional programs so that the major programs cover at least 30% of total federal awards expended
Audit additional programs so that the major programs cover at least 40% of total federal awards expended
items.rule_line: Major programs must cover at least 40% of awards expended, or 20% for a low-risk auditee.

why.A: The 20% coverage applies only when the auditee meets the criteria for a low-risk auditee, which Kestrel does not.
why.B: The required coverage is 40%, not 50%.
why.C: The required coverage is 40%, not 30%.
why.D: Correct. An auditee that is not low-risk requires coverage of at least 40% of total federal awards expended.

verify.note: 2 CFR 200.518(f): 저위험이면 20%, 아니면 40%. 정답 D 유효.

guide.ask: What coverage does a low-risk auditee need, and what applies otherwise?
guide.reveal: Lower coverage for low-risk auditees; a higher coverage percentage for others.

guide.ask: What is it for Kestrel?
guide.reveal: At least 40% of total federal awards expended, so more programs must be audited.
